name: cessna-open-loop
$comment: Open loop at 100 KTAS, 5000 ft: the five rigid-body modes of the c172p, one aircraft per mode. Generated by design/build_model.py; see the README.

annotations.text: **Airframe.** RigidBody3D at the centre of gravity of the POH gross loading (2400 lb, station 45.6 in), body axes x forward, y left, z up; Jxx, Jyy, Jzz = 2308, 1973, 3702 kg m^2 (the product Jxz 1.7 kg m^2 is neglected). Gravity is inside RigidBody3D.

**Power train (rotational bond graph).** The crankshaft 1-junction: the engine (PistonEngine, a torque source modulated by the throttle, the mixture and the manifold pressure), the crankshaft + propeller inertia (Rotor3D: the axial momentum, spinning about body x, on the airframe through RotorMount, so its torque reaction and gyroscopic moment act on the airframe) and the propeller (an R: torque over the shaft speed and the airspeed). The thrust and the propeller's aerodynamic torque act on the airframe at the hub (PropWrench).

**Open loop.** Five Cessnas trimmed at 100 KTAS, 5000 ft (alpha 2.14 deg, throttle 0.819, 2273 rpm, elevator 2.87 deg, mixture leaned for best power), each released on one eigenvector of the linearised model (design/c172_lin.py): SP short period (1 deg of alpha), Ph phugoid (2 m/s), DR dutch roll (1 deg of sideslip), Ro roll (2 deg of bank), Sl spiral (5 deg). The controls are held at the trim.

options.text: Five Cessnas trimmed at 100 KTAS, 5000 ft, each released on one eigenvector: the **short period** (1.3 s, well damped), the **phugoid** (25 s, lightly damped), the **dutch roll** (3 s), the **roll** subsidence (0.18 s) and the slow, stable **spiral**.
